channel.title: Dylan Gaeta: News
channel.description: Research, fieldwork, conferences, teaching, and milestones from Dylan Gaeta, Ph.D.

item.title: Launched snowdrought.org
item.description: Launched snowdrought.org, the Western US Climate and Snow Drought Explorer. An interactive dashboard of maps, time series, seasonal cycles, and cross-product anomalies of snow, water, carbon, and vegetation across the Western U.S. (1990–2026).

item.title: CIRES Science Summit
item.description: Spent the day at the CIRES Science Summit, an institute-wide meeting built around strengthening collaborations across CIRES divisions.

item.title: Paper published: U.S. oil and gas methane intensity, 2019–2024
item.description: Our paper U.S. oil and gas methane emission intensity declined 2019–2024 with little indication of federal policy impact came out in Communications Earth & Environment. Led by Ao Chen in the Greenhouse Gas Lab.

item.title: Preprint posted: progress toward China's methane goals
item.description: New preprint led by Ziting Huang: Satellite-based emissions estimate indicates progress toward China's methane mitigation goals, now in review at Communications Earth & Environment.

item.title: OCO-2 v11 MIP modeling workshop
item.description: Joined the OCO-2 v11 Model Intercomparison Project (MIP) modeling workshop with the atmospheric CO₂ flux inversion groups that assimilate OCO-2 retrievals. The MIP compares global flux estimates across inversion systems, including CarbonTracker from NOAA GML and CU Boulder.

item.title: GMAC 2026 poster: methyl bromide emissions
item.description: Presented A decline but no cessation of methyl bromide emissions from the United States over 2007–2018 at GMAC 2026, the 53rd NOAA Global Monitoring Annual Conference (abstract volume). Used tall tower, observatory, and aircraft flask-sample measurements of CH₃Br from the NOAA GGGRN with a geostatistical inverse model to estimate U.S. emissions across the Montreal Protocol phase-out years.

item.title: CIRES Rendezvous poster
item.description: Presented A decline in U.S. methyl bromide emissions throughout 2007–2021 at the 21st annual CIRES Rendezvous, CIRES's institute-wide science symposium. My first Rendezvous, about two months after starting at CIRES.

item.title: Johns Hopkins Science Diplomacy Summit
item.description: Attended the third annual Johns Hopkins Science Diplomacy Summit, which brought together government officials, researchers, and industry on AI, quantum, climate innovation, health, space, Arctic science, and research security.

item.title: Started my postdoc at CIRES and NOAA GML
item.description: Joined CIRES and the NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory as a Postdoctoral Research Associate, working with Dr. Aleya Kaushik on a NOAA/NIDIS-funded project. Focus: drought and carbon cycle dynamics in the Western U.S., combining NOAA GGGRN flask measurements, satellite data (FluxSat, TROPOMI, OCO-2, GRACE), ERA5-Land, and the SiB4 land surface model. CIRES profile

item.title: CCST structural fumigation report published
item.description: The California Council on Science and Technology's report on structural fumigation with sulfuryl fluoride, prepared for California's Department of Pesticide Regulation, draws on our 2024 paper and includes our U.S. emissions estimates.

item.title: Ph.D. complete
item.description: Officially completed my Ph.D. in Geography & Environmental Engineering at Johns Hopkins.

item.title: Paper published: Arctic and boreal methane fluxes
item.description: Our paper Methane fluxes from Arctic & boreal North America: comparisons between process-based estimates and atmospheric observations came out in Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics. Led by Hanyu Liu, comparing process-based methane flux estimates with atmospheric observations across Arctic and boreal North America.

item.title: Paper published: global wetland methane from satellites
item.description: Our paper Spatial and temporal distribution of global wetland methane emissions during 2019–2020 estimated from satellite observations came out in JGR Atmospheres, led by Ao Chen.

item.title: Defended my dissertation
item.description: Defended U.S. emissions of trace gas air pollutants inferred from a long-term atmospheric measurement network: from fumigants to fossil fuels. Three case studies using NOAA flask measurements and a geostatistical inverse model to map U.S. emissions: Sulfuryl fluoride: California dominates U.S. emissions, mostly from structural fumigation for drywood termites. Methyl bromide: emissions fell after the Montreal Protocol phase-out but not to zero, sustained by quarantine and pre-shipment uses and California strawberry growing. Propane, butane, and pentane: oil and gas basins dominate, led by the Permian, Anadarko, Eagle Ford, and Haynesville, with implications for ozone downwind.

item.title: Paper published: the ChiWIS instrument
item.description: The instrument paper for the Chicago Water Isotope Spectrometer, The airborne Chicago Water Isotope Spectrometer, came out in Atmospheric Measurement Techniques. Eight years after the 2017 StratoClim campaign in Nepal, where I worked with the ChiWIS team.

item.title: AIRDC workshop, hosted at Johns Hopkins
item.description: Attended the 3rd Annual Greater Washington, D.C. Air Quality Research and Development Consortium (AIRDC) Workshop, this year hosted by Johns Hopkins in Baltimore.

item.title: JHU Sustainability Symposium poster
item.description: Presented Tracking U.S. pesticide emissions using atmospheric measurements and inverse modeling at the JHU Sustainability Symposium. Brought the sulfuryl fluoride and methyl bromide work to a university-wide sustainability audience.

item.title: Started at Scale AI
item.description: Began working as a Human Frontier Collective Specialist (GenAI). Build evaluation frameworks and contribute climate science and atmospheric chemistry expertise to test and improve generative AI models.

item.title: Death Valley field course, year four
item.description: Co-led our 8-day Case Studies in Climate Change field course (EN.570.321) with Prof. Scot Miller for ten undergraduates. Route ran through Death Valley and up the Eastern Sierra, using the landscape to teach past, present, and future climate change in California. Fourth year of the trip.

item.title: Graduate Board Oral (GBO) exam
item.description: Passed my Graduate Board Oral exam and advanced to Ph.D. candidacy, with a dissertation plan built around fumigant and fossil fuel emissions.

item.title: AGU 2024: talk on C₃–C₅ alkanes, poster on methyl bromide
item.description: Gave an oral talk, Emissions of C₃–C₅ alkanes from the U.S. fossil fuel industry and implications for air quality (A42E-06). Presented a poster, U.S. emissions of methyl bromide have declined since the Montreal Protocol phase-out, but not to zero (A21H-1855). Two dissertation chapters presented at the same meeting.

item.title: BSEC annual meeting
item.description: Attended the annual meeting of the Baltimore Social-Environmental Collaborative (BSEC), the DOE-funded Urban Integrated Field Lab led by Johns Hopkins. BSEC brings together scientists from several universities and national labs with Baltimore communities to study urban climate, air, and water.

item.title: Paper published: OCO-2 and the seasonal carbon cycle
item.description: Our paper The Orbiting Carbon Observatory-2 (OCO-2) and in situ CO₂ data suggest a larger seasonal amplitude of the terrestrial carbon cycle compared to many dynamic global vegetation models came out in Remote Sensing of Environment, led by Ruixue Lei.

item.title: Paper published: U.S. ethane emissions
item.description: Our paper U.S. ethane emissions and trends estimated from atmospheric observations came out in Environmental Science & Technology, led by Mingyang Zhang.

item.title: Outstanding Doctoral TA Award
item.description: Received the department's Outstanding Doctoral TA Award.

item.title: AIRDC workshop at George Mason
item.description: Attended the 2nd Annual Greater Washington, D.C. Air Quality Research and Development Consortium (AIRDC) Workshop.

item.title: First first-author paper: sulfuryl fluoride
item.description: My first first-author paper is out in Communications Earth & Environment: California dominates U.S. emissions of the pesticide and potent greenhouse gas sulfuryl fluoride. California emits 60–85% of U.S. SO₂F₂ (0.26 ± 0.10 Gg/yr), equal to 5.5–12% of global emissions. Covered by The Guardian, the Los Angeles Times, Scientific American, The Hill, and others (media).

item.title: Paper published: transport variability and U.S. methane trends
item.description: Our paper Inter-annual variability in atmospheric transport complicates estimation of US methane emissions trends came out in Geophysical Research Letters, led by Leyang Feng.

item.title: Two awards from my department
